EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This Risk Management Plan Executive Summary was developed pursuant to Section 2745.3 of the California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program codified by Title 19, California Code of Regulations (CCR), Division 2, and Chapter 4.5. The purpose of this Executive Summary is to provide a brief description of certain elements of the Risk Management Plan that has been implemented at the Exquadrum, Inc. Forge Facility, located in Victorville, California. The objectives of the California Accidental Release Prevention Program  are to prevent the accidental release of certain regulated substances, minimize the risk to the community, and promote communication between the facility and emergency response personnel.  


1.0   ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION POLICIES
Exquadrum, Inc. has a long-standing commitment to worker and public safety.  This commitment is demonstrated by the resources invested in accident prevention, such as personnel training and consideration of safety in the design, operation, and maintenance of the covered processes.  Exquadrum, Inc. policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases of regulated substances.

The main operation of Exquadrum, Inc.s Forge Facility is to test and collect data on proposed rocket propulsion, engines, and motors. There are a number of chemicals of interest that are stored in chemical storage lockers and flammable cabinets including oxidizers and fuels.The chemical storage has two lockers, separating the fuels and oxidizers. These propellants are stored in 4BW DOT Containers. These are all well regulated, permitted, and inspected by local, county, and state officials. Any excess hazardous material is gathered and stored in separate containers at a specific location at the Forge Facility to be properly disposed of by a professional third party. All use, excess, and disposed of hazardous material is documented and kept on file for five years

Exquadrum, Incs Forge Facility uses t

he following chemicals in amounts that exceed the regulatory threshold for certain regulatory defined processes including:
 - Mixed Oxides of Nitrogen
 - Monomethylhydrazine
 - Hydrazine

3.0 HAZARD ASSESSMENT SUMMARY/OFFSITE CONSEQUENCE ANALYSIS
Worst-Case Release Scenario Results Summary for Toxics

Process 1 WCR Scenario Description: The worst-case scenario for Mixed oxides of nitrogen in the Chemical Storage Pad assumes a rupture and release of the entire contents of one 110-gal 4BW DOT container containing 110 gallons (1,331 lbs) of Mixed oxides of nitrogen, which spills and creates a liquid evaporating pool on the ground in the chemical storage pad. The air, ground, and puddle temperature used in the simulation is 110oF which is the highest average temperature in Victorville, California. Moreover, enclosure (unsheltered single storied building) was considered as a mitigation measure. Using the parameters mandated by regulations, the ALOHA Computer Code Application Guidance for Documented Safety Analysis, and the Average Weather in Victorville, California, this worst-case release has a total of 1331 lbs Mixed oxides of nitrogen released into the atmosphere with the potential to traverse a greater than 6-mile radius from the point of release and the potential to affect the population of 122 people.

Process 2 WCR Scenario Description:  The worst-case scenario for Monomethylhydrazine in the Chemical Storage Pad assumes a rupture and release of the entire contents of one 55-gal 4BW DOT container containing 50 gallons (365 lbs) of Monomethylhydrazine, in the chemical storage pad. The air temperature used in the simulation is 110oF which is the highest average temperature in Victorville, California. Moreover, enclosure (unsheltered single storied building) was considered as a mitigation measure. Using the parameters mandated by regulations, the ALOHA Computer Code Application Guidance for Documented Safety Analysis, and the Average Weather in Victorville, California

, this worst-case release has a total of 365 lbs Monomethylhydrazine released into the atmosphere with the potential to traverse a 5.9-mile radius from the point of release and the potential to affect the population of 69 people.

Process 3 WCR Scenario Description: The worst-case scenario for Hydrazine in the Chemical Storage Pad assumes a rupture and release of the entire contents of one 120-gal 4BW DOT container containing 120 gallons (1008 lbs) of Hydrazine, which spills and creates a liquid evaporating pool on the ground in the chemical storage pad. The air, ground, and puddle temperature used in the simulation is 110oF which is the highest average temperature in Victorville, California. Moreover, enclosure (unsheltered single storied building) was considered as a mitigation measure. Using the parameters mandated by regulations, the ALOHA Computer Code Application Guidance for Documented Safety Analysis, and the Average Weather in Victorville, California, this worst-case release has a total of 1008 lbs Hydrazine released into the atmosphere with the potential to traverse a greater than 6-mile radius from the point of release and the potential to affect the population of 126 people.

Alternative Release Scenario Results Summary for Toxics

Process 1 ARS Scenario Description: The alternative release scenario considers a pipe rupture during the transfer from the 4 BW DOT container to the Run Tank in the VTS 2 Testing Pad to be the most probable scenario that could happen. A total of 110 gallons (1,331 lbs) of Mixture of Oxides and Nitrogen is assumed to be released within a 10-minute duration in the Testing Pad. The liquid temperature used in the simulation is 110oF which is the highest daily temperature in Victorville, California. No mitigation measure was considered for this alternative release. Using the parameters mandated by regulations through RMP*Comp program, this alternative release has a total of 1,331 lbs Mixture of Oxides and Nitrogen released into the

atmosphere with the potential to traverse a 0.8-mile radius from the point of release and the potential to affect a population of 0 people.

4.0 ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS
As part of the implementation of this Risk Management Program, key Prevention Program elements were implemented by Exquadrum Inc. to manage process safety issues associated with the covered processes. In addition, common industry standards, policies, and procedures are currently utilized to ensure safe practices are being performed.
Exquadrum Inc. Forge facilit

y's CalARP Prevention Program 3 elements for the toxic substances, Mixed oxides of nitrogen, Monomethylhydrazine, and hydrazine, include: 
Common Elements of CalARP Prevention Program 3
 - Process Safety Information
 - Process Hazard Analysis
 - Operating Procedures
 - Training
 - Mechanical Integrity
 - Management of Change
 - Pre-Startup Safety Review
 - Compliance Audits
 - Incident Investigation
 - Employee Participation
 - Hot Work Permits
 - Contractors
 - Emergency Planning & Response

5.0 FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
Prior to the delivery date of this document, there have been no CalARP Program-related accidents at the Exquadrum Inc in the past five (5) years.  An incident investigation procedure is kept onsite which summarizes the required data that will be used as necessary to document any CalARP Program-related incidents.

6.0 EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
Exquadrum Inc. is committed to providing a safe and healthful work environment for its employees, the surrounding community, and the environment. The prevention of accidents, injuries, fires, emergency releases, and other emergency situations is of utmost importance and shall be the first priority for all persons working at the refinery.
Exquadrum Inc. is not a first responder. Thus, Exquadrum Inc. has an Emergency Action Plan in place and submits appropriate documentation regarding the chemicals and associated quantities to be included in the community emergency response plan.

7.0 PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
The planned changes to improve safety at the facility resolve the recommendations derived from the Process Hazard Analysis, as well as incorporated recommendations from compliance audits and incident investigations, as they become available.  The facility has a tracking system for implementing these recommendations and ensuring its closure. As required by the regulations, recommendations will be addressed and closed in a timely manner.
